title: Service account bootstrap templates and owner onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a minimal, auditable, and repeatable bootstrap flow for creating service accounts with least-privilege templates and a clear owner-onboarding UX for both Console and CLI. This ticket delivers: 1) a small set of canonical JSON/YAML templates for common service account roles (pipeline-runner, model-inference, metrics-exporter), 2) Console + CLI flow to select a template, scope resources, and assign an owner, and 3) automatic audit tags and owner TTL (time-to-live) enforcement to reduce orphaned accounts.

Background: Multiple incidents and customer feedback showed service accounts being created with excessive scopes and without clear owners. Existing guardrails were ad-hoc and inconsistent across Console and automation. RBAC v2 aims to centralize policy manifests; this work focuses on onboarding and templating as a first-class surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Three canonical templates implemented and stored in the policy repo (pipeline-runner, inference-worker, observability-scraper).
- Console flow: create service account -> select template -> confirm resource scope override (if allowed) -> assign owner (user or team) -> optional TTL -> create; UI must display policy diff before creation.
- CLI flow: redwood sa create --template=inference-worker --owner=team-ml --ttl=30d creates identical account and emits an audit event.
- Audit log entries must include: template_id, owner, creator, TTL, applied_override (if any), and checksum of effective privileges. Tag format: sa.template=<id>;sa.owner=<owner>.
- Onboarding step triggers owner-notification email (or Slack) with link to manage the SA.
- Orphan detection: background job marks SAs without owners after TTL window and creates a review issue in Console.

Design choices & trade-offs:
- Template granularity: We intentionally limit to a small set of curated templates to reduce combinatorial explosion. More templates can be added after analysis of usage patterns.
- Overrides: Allow resource-scope overrides only when operators have an explicit approval label. This keeps a balance between developer speed and least-privilege. Overrides are recorded and flagged in audits.
- TTL enforcement vs. mandatory owner: TTL is optional to avoid breaking automation but we require assigning either an individual or a team owner at creation.

Implementation notes:
- Template storage: YAML files in infra/policy/service-account-templates/ in the monorepo. Schema: template_id, description, allowed_scopes (list), default_scopes (list), recommended_ttl_days (int), approval_required (boolean).
- Backend: extend identity-service endpoints: POST /service-accounts with template_id and override payload; validate against policy engine. New DB columns: template_id (string), owner_id (string), ttl_days (int), override_checksum (string).
- Audit: Emit structured audit events to the audit-log service with the specified tags. Ensure events are indexed in our ELK cluster for queries like sa.template:inference-worker AND sa.owner:team-ml.
- Console: Add a single modal driven flow and a policy diff renderer (reuse existing policy diff component). Reuse identity-service client and the new audit tagging fields.
- CLI: Add a subcommand redwood sa create with aliases to mirror Console. Use same validation calls to avoid drift.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for template schema validation and backend validation paths.
- Integration tests that create SAs via CLI and Console stubs and assert audit events in test audit sink.
- E2E smoke tests: create -> assign owner -> verify owner notification stub -> TTL expiration background job behavior.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge templates and API changes behind feature flag sa-templates-v1.
2) Internal Canary: enable for Redwood dev tenants for 2 weeks. Monitor audit events, template usage, and support tickets.
3) Open beta for opt-in customers; collect feedback and add 1–2 templates that customers request.
4) GA: flip feature flag, deprecate old ad-hoc flows, and publish migration guide.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require team owners to be backed by an internal team object (preferred) or allow free-form owner strings? (Preference: team object to enable on-call rotations).
- What is the default TTL for templates that recommend one? (Propose 30 days for ephemeral workloads).
- Who approves overrides in practice? Build an approval label + audit trail; need product decision on approver roles.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/security/service-account-templates (design doc)
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1045 (template schema + initial templates)
- Console mock: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/sa-template-mockup-2026 (UI flows)
- Incident reference: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/2025-11-orphan-sa (lessons)

Security considerations:
- Ensure KMS keys used by SAs inherit customer KMS usage policy for Private deployments.
- Prevent template authorship from granting clandestine scopes; template commits must require security review.
- Ensure audit events do not leak secrets; only include identifiers and checksums.

Next steps (short term):
- Create template files in infra/policy (ENG-35722 will own adding the three canonical templates).
- Backend API schema PR (ENG-35723) to add DB columns and validation.
- Console modal prototype (DES-1287) for UX review.
- Schedule security review in the next security sync (due 2026-02-25).
